score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on adopted London waste policy, current GLA circular-economy guidance and official DEFRA/Environment Agency waste-classification and duty-of-care guidance.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI7
sources.fact: Adopted policy promotes circular economy and waste prevention; it includes targets for zero biodegradable/recyclable waste to landfill by 2026, 65% municipal recycling by 2030 and 95% construction/demolition reuse-recycling-recovery.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI8
sources.fact: Adopted policy sets net waste self-sufficiency and requires safeguarding/optimising waste capacity; strategic capacity does not prove a specific site can accept waste.

sources.label: Circular Economy Statement Guidance
sources.fact: Guidance puts retention, adaptation, reuse and high-value material recovery into design and applies to referable schemes while encouraging borough use for smaller developments.

sources.label: Circular Economy Statement detailed guidance
sources.fact: Statements address demolition/remediation reuse, design for disassembly, waste storage/collection, expected waste and monitoring; compliance requires complete and technically valid commitments.

sources.label: Whole Life-Cycle Carbon guidance
sources.fact: Whole-life carbon includes materials, construction, use, demolition and disposal; a scheme-specific assessment is needed rather than generic material assumptions.

sources.label: DEFRA waste hierarchy guidance
sources.fact: Official guidance sets the waste hierarchy and how businesses/public bodies generating, handling or treating waste should apply it.

sources.label: Waste duty of care code of practice
sources.fact: Duty of care requires lawful, safe waste management and accurate transfer descriptions/classification; construction and demolition waste is within scope.

sources.label: Classify different types of waste
sources.fact: Environment Agency/DEFRA collection published 1 May 2025 covers legal responsibilities, WM3 and construction/demolition waste classification.

sources.label: Hazardous waste hierarchy guidance
sources.fact: Hazardous-waste producers and holders have specific hierarchy obligations; hazardous status cannot be inferred from generic construction activity.

sources.label: Planning Practice Guidance collection
sources.fact: National planning practice guidance must be read with the NPPF; generic planning policy does not replace current waste permitting or scheme evidence.

sources.label: GLA Design for a Circular Economy
sources.fact: GLA design material promotes embedding circular-economy principles in built-environment projects; it is guidance/context, not a waste-transfer record.

sources.label: GLA Circular Economy Statements EqIA
sources.fact: The assessment links circular-economy implementation to reduced resource demand, waste transport and emissions; these are strategic effects rather than parcel-specific quantified savings.

examples.result: SI7 recycling/recovery targets are policy targets and are not applied as a site-specific achieved rate without records.
SI8 London-wide waste-capacity policy does not establish availability at a particular facility or date.
Circular Economy Statements require actual scheme commitments; no demolition/reuse percentage is invented.
Waste hierarchy evidence is retained separately from planning permission and from environmental permitting.
Duty-of-care transfer/classification requirements block generic assumptions about destination and lawful handling.
WM3/official classification is required where applicable; no hazardous/non-hazardous label is filled from land-use type alone.
Strategic circular-economy benefits are not converted into cost, carbon or viability savings without scheme evidence.
No waste/circular-economy promotion occurs without exact development scope, waste streams and current evidence.
